pages.text: "Grandma, look! The biggest chestnut!" Leo the know-it-all fox held a chestnut high. Grandma held her baby bear grandchild and patted gently. "Shh. The baby is sleeping."
"But mine is the biggest..." Leo's voice grew soft. He went to the other side of the stove and turned his back. "That little thing can't do anything."
Grandma put chestnuts on the stove. Pop, pop, they began to cook. The baby bear opened its eyes and cried. Grandma held a long wooden stick.
"Oh dear, only two hands." Grandma looked between the baby and the stove. The crying grew louder. With his back turned, Leo fiddled only with his chestnut.
The crying wouldn't stop. Leo set down the chestnut and quietly came around the stove. The baby waved both arms high.
As Leo turned, his long tail swept before the baby. The baby stopped crying and held the tail tip tight. Those little hands were warm.
Leo tried swishing his tail gently. The baby laughed and turned its head to follow. "Big brother's tail—swish, swish!" Leo's muzzle lifted into a smile.
Turning the chestnuts, Grandma asked, "Leo, what is the baby holding?" "My tail!" Leo stood proud. "Even ten gentle rocks from me didn't make this baby laugh."
Leo made himself a place by the stove. "One, come close gently! Two, swish my tail! Three, if the baby laughs, once more!" Now the baby's eyes followed only Leo.

Grandma hugged Leo and the baby bear together. "Our lodge has a big brother now." With a little one around, there is something only you can do. "Big brother's tail—swish, swish!" Leo waved his tail again.
